{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeqGzWw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhILT_U", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 365, "title": "Move Web microphone controls to toolbar context menu and add microphone position preference", "body": "## Goal

Move **Web microphone** control out of **Graph Library** and into the **Chrome extension toolbar icon's native right-click (action context) menu**, where users naturally expect extension-wide settings. Also allow users to choose the position of the **microphone button shown beside editable fields on websites**.

**This is about the injected Web microphone button next to text fields, not moving the Chrome toolbar icon itself.** Do not create a new general-purpose Options page (it was removed by #318) or turn this into a separate UI/settings surface.

## Desired toolbar context menu

Add these entries to the existing right-click menu for the **My Audio to Text** toolbar action:

- **Web microphone** — a native checkable ON/OFF menu item, reflecting the saved feature enablement state. This controls the presence of the Web microphone button on supported websites; it must **not** start recording.
- **Microphone position** — a submenu of native radio items:
  - **Auto** (default): prefer the right side of the active editable field; fall back to left when necessary;
  - **Left**: prefer the field's left side;
  - **Right**: prefer the field's right side.
- Preserve the existing **Graphs → Open → [graph]** and **Graphs → Graph Library** menu hierarchy and the current primary-click behavior (launch Live graph).

Keep this menu compact, using Chrome's native checkbox/radio presentation rather than custom decorative copy, extra popups, or a permanent help banner.

## Current implementation (main branch as inspected 2026-11-12)

- [`extension/background.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/background.js) already registers native `chrome.contextMenus` on the `action` context, rebuilds the menu via `refreshMenus()`, and supports the **Graphs** subtree. It calls `chrome.contextMenus.removeAll()` when refreshing: the new microphone items need to be reconstructed and kept in sync, not lost on graph updates.
- [`extension/graph-library-page.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library-page.js) currently owns `#web-voice-enabled` and the ON/OFF permission, storage and reconciliation workflow. [`extension/graph-library.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library.html) contains the current toggle/help UI.
- [`extension/web-voice-preference.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-preference.js) stores the `web-voice-typing-v1` opt-in in `chrome.storage.local`.
- [`extension/web-voice-background.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-background.js) handles feature reconciliation, optional website access, dynamic content-script registration/unregistration, stopping active sessions, and offscreen runtime lifecycle.
- [`extension/web-voice-content.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/web-voice-content.js) displays a floating microphone beside an editable target. Its `position()` currently places it **right-first, else left near viewport edge**, with viewport clamps/transforms/modal handling.
- The microphone icon itself is still clicked inside the website to begin/stop recording. Its right-click menu currently chooses a default compatible voice graph; **preserve this separate per-field functionality**.

## Required changes

### 1) Control feature enablement from the toolbar context menu

1. Add a checkable **Web microphone** item at the top level of the extension toolbar right-click menu, with the check state synchronized to the canonical saved preference and effective permissions.
2. **ON:** request optional `http://*/*` / `https://*/*` host permissions when needed, with explicit Chrome user consent, then enable/reconcile dynamic website content scripts and the current feature state. Respect Chrome's requirement for a user-initiated `chrome.permissions.request` flow; if a native context menu click cannot reliably show a permission prompt in a supported Chrome configuration, use the smallest explicit, user-initiated extension consent surface or other browser-supported flow, rather than silently failing, over-granting, or reintroducing a general Options page.
3. **OFF:** immediately stop/abort active Web voice-typing sessions and capture, remove the floating page microphone controls, unregister scripts, and persist OFF. Handle/recover cleanly if a preference write or reconciliation fails; never present ON as successfully enabled before it actually is.
4. Ensure repeated clicks, pending permission dialogs, permissions removed externally, other tabs, service worker restarts, and async menu refreshes cannot leave the checkbox visibly out of sync with real state. Use the existing canonical preference and reconciliation logic rather than creating a second conflicting ON/OFF flag.
5. **Do not start microphone capture on menu ON.** Continue to request/use the site microphone only when a user intentionally clicks the injected button on the editable field, as currently implemented.
6. Remove the **Web microphone ON/OFF** toggle and its dedicated controls/help from **Graph Library**. Do not replace it there with persistent instructions or a redirect to the menu; Library remains for graph management. Keep access to relevant graph editing/selection functionality.

### 2) Choose microphone button placement

7. Add a native **Microphone position** submenu to the toolbar context menu with mutually exclusive **Auto**, **Left**, and **Right** radio items. **Auto is the default**, matching the current right-first behavior.
8. Persist the chosen placement centrally (e.g. `chrome.storage.local`, with a distinct setting key), validate stored values, and restore the correct checked radio on startup/rebuilds. No per-page setting UI.
9. Update `web-voice-content.js` placement to follow the preference **relative to the focused editable field**:
   - Auto: prefer right; fall back to left when needed (as today).
   - Left: prefer left, but fall back/clamp when the field is at an edge.
   - Right: prefer right, but fall back/clamp when the field is at an edge.
   The position setting is a **preference**, not a reason to put an active control offscreen or behind a modal.
10. Keep robust viewport bounding, zoom, scrolling, resized fields, iframe/top-frame rules, transformed containers, shadow DOM, modal/top-layer behavior, and easy access to **Stop/Cancel** while a recording is active. Changes should update visible idle microphone position without requiring a browser restart or losing editable-field caret/selection.
11. Setting position while the microphone feature is OFF should be allowed and should apply when it is next enabled.

### 3) Integrate without regressions

12. Preserve **Graphs → Open** (selected graph radio states), **Graphs → Graph Library**, the primary toolbar click launching a Live window, and the **website microphone's own right-click graph selection**.
13. Update relevant user-facing error messages referencing “Turn ON in Graph Library” / “Enable Web voice typing in Graph Library” to give an accurate and concise action through the toolbar context menu, **only when an error actually occurs**.
14. Avoid any new persistent explanations, duplicated toggles, generic notifications or broader microphone preferences beyond the requested position setting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Right-clicking the Chrome extension toolbar icon shows a checkable **Web microphone** item and **Microphone position → Auto / Left / Right** radio submenu, alongside existing Graphs entries.
- [ ] Web microphone OFF by default for a new install; first ON follows a real explicit optional website-permission consent flow and succeeds only when permission is granted.
- [ ] ON shows the Web microphone button next to eligible website text fields, **without starting recording**. OFF reliably removes the buttons and terminates active Web voice sessions/capture.
- [ ] Graph Library no longer shows the Web microphone ON/OFF control or redundant supporting help.
- [ ] The menu check/radio states persist across extension restarts, open windows, menu rebuilds and permissions changes; denied permission/failed writes do not display falsely enabled state.
- [ ] Auto/Left/Right visibly alter microphone placement relative to the editable field; field-edge constraints, zoom, scrolling, focus, and recording Stop/Cancel controls remain safe and usable.
- [ ] Changing placement live updates controls when possible without interfering with typing, text selection, or caret position.
- [ ] The native toolbar icon primary click, Graphs menus and the injected microphone's context graph selection continue to work.
- [ ] Automated browser/unit tests cover menu actions, first-time permission granted/denied paths, state synchronization, disable/abort cleanup, placement choices/fallback, and existing graph-menu regressions. No manual approval gate.

## Likely files

- `extension/background.js` — context menu creation/refresh/click handling.
- `extension/web-voice-background.js` / `extension/web-voice-preference.js` — canonical consent, enablement and storage/reconcile.
- `extension/web-voice-content.js` — placement preference and live repositioning.
- `extension/graph-library-page.js`, `extension/graph-library.html` — remove misplaced Web microphone switch/help.
- Web microphone / toolbar context menu / content-injection tests and any relevant docs.

## Design principle

**Graph Library is for managing graphs; the extension toolbar context menu is for extension-wide microphone UI enablement and positioning.** Use browser-native menu controls. Keep the microphone recording opt-in separate from the global visibility setting.
